Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-12 - blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context before or during this task gave a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this fragment. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-042 in packet-12. I did not read packet.json and did not use any search tool. Proper names and a rubric are visible in the text itself (see below). I report them as readings only and have not tried to identify the work.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations only)
======================================================================

Face A (image-001 overview; tiles image-002 to image-021):
- A parchment bifolium photographed open and flat, with sewing holes and stitching at the central fold. Both halves are written in ONE column each. There are about 45 long lines per page, ruled in drypoint/plummet, with double vertical bounding lines and double horizontal lines at the head and foot.
- Script: a small Gothic textualis book hand in brown-black ink, with heavy abbreviation (2-shaped et "z", -orum hook, q(uo)d, p(er)/p(re)/p(ro) bars, superscript vowels). The left page is clean. The right page is heavily stained, and its inner (left) third is badly faded.
- Rubrication: red paragraph marks (a "C"-shaped red sign) introduce new sections. On the left page one appears at "Igit(ur) dum aurora". On the right page they appear at "Mulier quedam Gerdrudis", "Vir quida(m) no(m)i(n)e hainric(us)", "Puella q(ue)dam Mehtildis", "Mulier quedam Treuensis", "Vir quidam ... moguntin(e)", plus a red touch at "Que cum iussa". There are red touches on some capitals (Traduntur, "Tunc almatius", "Et cecilia", "Cum adh(oc)"). Near the foot of the right page is a two-line red rubric in the text column, to the right: "De nomine / s(an)c(t)e cecilie". Below it a large red initial C opens a new section ("[C]ecilia q(ua)si celi lilia...").
- Marginalia:
  (a) Left page, outer margin, opposite text line 19 (image-007 about line 12): a small later note, partly read: "fra[t?]n[i?]t[..]" (possibly a gloss or expansion of "fr(atern)itatis" in the text line; uncertain).
  (b) Left page, outer margin, opposite text line 32 (image-012 about line 8): a small note, read tentatively as "a[p]paritoribus". It sits beside the text word "apitonib(us)", which seems to carry a line through or over it (possibly a correction; uncertain).
  (c) Right page, outer margin, beside the "De nomine s(an)c(t)e cecilie" rubric (image-016): a later note in a different hand, "+ / Defectu(s?) [..] / in fine lib(ri?)". There is a cross or signe-de-renvoi above it. The reading of "[..]" and "lib(ri?)" is uncertain.
  (d) Lower margin of the left page, written UPSIDE DOWN relative to the text (image-001, image-017, image-018, image-019): two lines of large later calligraphic Gothic/fraktur-like display script in brown ink, presumably from reuse as a binding or cover. I did not attempt a confident reading. Read inverted, the upper line seems to begin with "S(?) ..." and the lower line contains something like "...b[e]rtholl[..]..."; treat both as [illegible] for matching purposes.
  (e) A modern oval paper label "IV. / 56." (shelf or numbering label) is stuck over the inverted inscription near the fold (image-019).
  (f) Modern pencil at the lower right of the right page: "Stams, StA, Frg. 222r" (image-020, image-021).
- Damage: there are holes or patches in the right page near the "De nomine" rubric (image-015) and at the bottom line. Inside the larger hole, text from a different layer (an underlying or offset leaf) shows, with fragments such as "...nnilio(?)", "...atione ma...", "...ut xpi med...", "...ntia (?)pu...". These do not belong to the main text line. A small hole in the right page line "...dyoc[hole] cu(m) lumine ocu..." (image-010, image-011). Water and dirt staining covers the whole right page, and its left third is faded almost to illegibility.

Face B (image-022 overview; tiles image-023 to image-042):
- The other side is covered by a pasted paper lining/pastedown (laid paper with visible fibres). There is NO medieval text visible on it. Along the spine, under or through the torn paper, a narrow strip of a later music manuscript shows (five-line staves with round-headed notes, beams and stems; image-025, image-030, image-035, image-040). This is a binding strip, not part of the parchment text. Modern pencil at lower right: "Stams, STA, Frg. 222v" (image-042). Paper lifting at the lower left (image-039, image-040). There is nothing to transcribe on face B.

Tentative interpretation (not an identification): continuous narrative prose (dialogue with "Cui prefectus", "Cui ualianus", "Cui almatius") on the left page. On the right page, a series of short miracle reports, each opened by a paragraph mark. A new section with a "De nomine..." rubric then begins with a name etymology. There are no glosses or commentary layers; it is a single text.

======================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED
======================================================================
- Left page: the whole page, read from image-003 (top lines), image-008 (middle), image-013 (lower), with image-002/007/012 (left edges and margin) and image-004/009/014/019 (right ends of lines) for line ends.
- Right page: the whole page, read from image-005 (top), image-010 (middle), image-015 (lower), with image-006/011/016/021 for line ends and image-004/009/014 for the faded line beginnings. The first one to three words of most right-page lines are faint and only partly read.
- Unread: the inverted display inscription in the lower margin (only described). Face B has no text.

Overlaps: image-003 L8-L11 = image-008 L1-L4. image-008 L18-L21 = image-013 L1-L4. image-005 L9-L12 = image-010 L1-L4. image-010 L18-L21 = image-015 L1-L4. I transcribe overlapping lines once and note the duplicates. I complete line ends from the neighbouring right-hand tile (marked "|>" where a line end comes from the next tile).

Conventions: expansions in ( ); uncertain reading followed by (?); [illegible] or [gap] for unread or blank stretches; z = Tironian et / 2-shaped et as written; ¶ = red paragraph mark.

======================================================================
3. TRANSCRIPTION - FACE A, LEFT PAGE (one column)
======================================================================

image-003 (lines 1-11; line 1 is the first line of the page; line starts confirmed in image-002)

003.02  mente tua loquaris. Tunc iubet astare ualianum dicens ei. Q(uonia)m n(on) e(st) sani capitis fra
003.03  ter tuus. tu saltem pot(er)is sapiens dare responsum. Constat plurimum uos errare. qui
